title: Stratified finite-free calculation for completed rational pullback
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $\ell$ a prime invertible in $k$, and $X$ a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Fix an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ and finite intermediate fields $E\subset L$ over $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Write $A_E=\mathcal O_E$, choose a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and put $B_{E,X}=\varprojlim_{n\ge1}(A_E/\varpi_E^n)_X$ and $E_X=B_{E,X}[1/\varpi_E]$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. These are the continuous completed coefficient sheaves on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use the derived-complete constructible integral categories with compatible etale-origin witnesses [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], their raw rationalizations $D^b_c(X,E)$ [def-weil-pbc-rational-category], their bounded localized standard t-structures [prop-weil-localized-tstructure], and the pair category $D^b_c(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category], with the finite scalar functors $T_{L/E}$ and associators of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension].

Let $Y$ also be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme and let $g:Y\to X$ be any scheme morphism. For $\Lambda=E$ or $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, use the finite-stage or common-stage standard structure, respectively [lem-per-adic-common-stage-truncations]. The completed integral pullback [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] preserves the constructible complete categories, including their finite reduction witnesses; it rationalizes to an exact triangulated functor and has coherent comparisons with finite scalar extension, including the unit, composition and shift equations. Its common-stage descent is likewise an exact triangulated functor $Lg^*:D^b_c(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)\to D^b_c(Y,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$.

At a finite stage, let $J_X$ be the continuous rational realization [lem-per-continuous-rational-derived-realization]. If $F$ is a constructible $E_X$-module sheaf, and $S\hookrightarrow X$ is any stratum on which it is locally finite free, the restriction of $J_Y(Lg^*J_X^{-1}F)$ to $Y\times_X S$ is concentrated in degree zero. On the pullback of any pro-etale chart trivializing $F|_S$ as $E_S^r$, it is the finite free continuous target module of rank $r$ in degree zero, with its balanced-tensor identification. These assertions include empty strata and rank zero and impose no flatness hypothesis on $g^{-1}E_X\to E_Y$.

Consequently $Lg^*$ preserves the standard heart and both standard halves for both $\Lambda$. More generally it preserves every cohomological interval. Its restriction to the heart is exact, and the canonical truncation comparisons identify $\mathcal H^j(Lg^*K)$ with $g^*\mathcal H^j(K)$ for every integer $j$, compatibly with the finite scalar comparisons.

proof.text: Both $X$ and $Y$ satisfy the noetherian and finite-dimensional hypotheses of the cited adic results. Apply the finite-type noetherian theorem to their structure maps to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ (a field is noetherian). Apply the finite-type fibre dimension bound to the same maps: their unique fibres are $X$ and $Y$. The base is quasi-compact. Invertibility of $\ell$ is inherited from $k$. No smoothness, flatness or assumption that $k$ is algebraically closed is used.

proof.text: For each finite $E$, apply [lem-per-integral-pullback-bounds] to $g$. It gives constructible preservation with compatible reduction witnesses, the specified completion-unit isomorphism, linear exactness, and preservation of the integral halves and every ambient interval.

source.place: Lemma 6.5.9(4)-(5), Proposition 6.6.11; old proof steps 2-4: exact completed pullback and local-to-global integral cohomological bounds

proof.text: Step 2 makes each $\widehat P_{g,E}$ an $A_E$-linear exact functor of the constructible categories. Semilinear localization with $R=S=A_E$, $t=u=\varpi_E$ and $\phi=\mathrm{id}$ extends it to the exact functor $F_E$ with $F_E(f/\varpi_E^n)=\widehat P_{g,E}(f)/\varpi_E^n$. The scalar-extension package gives the exact transitions $T_{L/E}$ (with $T_{E/E}=\mathrm{id}$, associators and shift comparisons) and the ambient comparisons $C_{L/E,Y}\widehat P_{g,E}\cong\widehat P_{g,L}C_{L/E,X}$ with their identity, composition, tower and shift equations. By Step 2 these restrict to the constructible categories, and localization makes them exact isomorphisms $\beta_{L/E}:T_{L/E,Y}F_E\cong F_LT_{L/E,X}$ satisfying the same equations. The descent-functor proposition then gives the exact functor $F_\Omega(E,K)=(E,F_EK)$, sending a common-stage arrow $u$ over $L$ to $\beta_{\mathrm{target}}^{-1}F_L(u)\beta_{\mathrm{source}}$, independently of representatives. These are the stated completed pullbacks.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14 and Remark 6.8.15; old proof steps 5-6: scalar localization, restricted scalar comparisons and common-stage arrow action

proof.text: Apply coefficient-stage descent to these integral functors. Step 2 gives its integral exactness and half-preservation hypotheses; Step 3 gives its transitions and exact scalar comparisons. The localized structures have image halves; common-stage truncations give t-exact transitions and finite-stage halves and truncations. The pair-category definition and Verdier theorem give its triangulated pair categories and finite-stage triangles. Hence pullback is t-exact at every finite stage and at the algebraic closure, with exact heart restrictions and normalized truncation and cohomology comparisons commuting with scalar extension. Define $g^*$ as the heart restriction and invert the last comparison to obtain the stated direction. Each interval is the intersection of the corresponding shifted halves; the empty interval contains only zero.

proof.text: Given $F$ and its chosen integral-rational representative, [lem-per-rational-stratum-pullback-models] gives the restriction comparison on $Y\times_XS$, its degree-zero assertion, and on every pulled-back trivializing chart exactly the displayed finite free continuous module with the balanced-tensor map. It explicitly includes rank zero and empty strata without coefficient flatness.
